screenSummary.playArea: Two vectors u and w, their combination c₁u + c₂w, and optionally their span.
screenSummary.controlArea: Drag u and w, set c₁ and c₂, show the span, or try to hit a target.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Can every point be reached? When can't it?

controls.independent: Independent: {u, w} is a basis of ℝ²
controls.dependent: Dependent: the span is a line

screenSummary.playArea: The grid, unit square and letter F transformed by matrix A.
screenSummary.controlArea: Drag where î and ĵ land, edit A, pick a preset, morph from I to A, or compose with B.
screenSummary.interactionHint: What does the determinant measure? What happens when it is 0 or negative?

controls.handle1: Image of î (first column of A)
controls.handle2: Image of ĵ (second column of A)
controls.collapsed: Plane collapsed onto a line or a point

screenSummary.playArea: Ax = b shown as two lines, or as columns of A combining to make b.
screenSummary.controlArea: Edit A and b, switch pictures, and step through row reduction.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Why don't row operations move the solution?

controls.none: No solution: the lines are parallel
controls.contradiction: No solution: a row gives a contradiction

screenSummary.playArea: A vector v and its image Av; eigen-directions where they line up.
screenSummary.controlArea: Turn v, sweep it around, show eigenvectors, or iterate A.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Find the directions that A only stretches.

controls.unaligned: v and Av point different ways
controls.scalar: λ = {{value}}: every vector is an eigenvector

screenSummary.playArea: Vector b, its projection p onto the line through a, and the error e; or data with its least-squares line.
screenSummary.controlArea: Drag a and b, or drag data points and compare your own line.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Why is the error perpendicular to the line?

controls.distance: ‖e‖ = {{value}}: the shortest distance from b to the line
controls.bestFit: Best fit y = m x + k with m = {{slope}}, k = {{intercept}}
controls.projectionNote: The fitted values ŷ are the projection of y onto Col(X)
controls.allXEqual: All x equal: no unique line

screenSummary.playArea: A vector x in the standard grid and in the grid of basis b₁, b₂.
screenSummary.controlArea: Drag b₁, b₂ and x, or use A's eigenvectors as the basis.
screenSummary.interactionHint: What do x's coordinates look like in the new basis?

controls.useEigenvectors: Use eigenvectors of A as the basis
controls.diagonal: [A]<sub>B</sub> is diagonal: b₁, b₂ are eigenvectors of A
controls.parallel: b₁ and b₂ are parallel: not a basis

screenSummary.playArea: The unit circle carried by Vᵀ, Σ and U onto the ellipse A makes.
screenSummary.controlArea: Edit A, scrub or play the three stages, or show the grid.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Which directions become the axes of the ellipse?
